editorial.headline: Non-Ferrous Metal Rolling With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 24203 covers hot and cold rolling of non-ferrous metals, and the record marks it as nationally foreign-open and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 24203 is the activity code for rolling non-ferrous metals: not the broad romance of “metal industry,” but the more exact work of turning copper, aluminium, silver, zinc, magnesium, tin, and platinum into plates, sheets, strips, foils, and related forms. The record covers both hot rolling and cold rolling. It also reaches into the finishing and forming steps that produce metal wire, including drawing, tempering, and stressing, whether the wire is single or stranded, and whether or not it functions as an electrical conductor.

That makes the code most relevant to businesses whose actual registered activity is the milling and rolling of non-ferrous metal inputs into these intermediate metal products. The examples in the record are practical and industrial: copper plate, aluminium plate, copper sheet, aluminium sheet, silver strip, zinc strip, aluminium strip, magnesium sheet, tin foil, and platinum strip. The emphasis is on the process and output form. If the business is built around this rolling, forming, and wire-making scope, this is the activity being described.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as open to the activity, so the code is not presented as belonging only to large industrial operators. A registrant may sit at any of those listed business scales, provided the activity itself matches the scope. That matters because this is a process-led classification: the decisive question is not how glossy the business looks from outside, but whether the registered activity is the rolling of non-ferrous metals and the related wire-forming processes described in the record.

The national foreign-ownership picture is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership recorded is 100%. In plain English, the slim record treats this code as nationally open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason: the record marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says, verbatim, “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this code is not flagged as blocked. So the honest reading is direct: for KBLI 24203, the record shows a nationally foreign-open activity and no Bali moratorium block today.
